title: Gated model onboarding pipeline with signed provenance and auto-pinning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Build an end-to-end CI/CD pipeline that automates model artifact creation, cryptographic signing, provenance publishing, automated performance profiling, and catalog pin promotion with canary gating and auto-rollback. The pipeline should produce a reproducible model artifact (model.bin + manifest), sign artifacts and metadata, publish attestations to our provenance registry, run the standard perf suite and QA tests, and open or update a GitOps PR to the model-catalog to change the pinned version for staged and stable channels. Gate promotion on explicit perf/regression thresholds and metadata checks. On regressions or failing health checks during canary, automatically revert the pin and publish a rollback incident note.

Goals:
- Remove manual steps for model onboarding and pin promotion across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Ensure every published model version has cryptographic provenance and a perf profile attached.
- Provide a safe canary path with automated rollback if perf or quality falls below thresholds.
- Produce traceable audit artifacts (signed manifest, SBOM-like metadata, benchmark runs, PR history).

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: build job templates (GHA/CloudBuild), signing integration (cosign-like or internal KMS attestation), publishing to artifact registry and provenance index, perf runner harness wired into CI, GitOps PR flow for model-catalog, canary rollout automation and automated rollback.
- Out of scope: major refactor of existing model runtime; long-term UI work for console (Console UX follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI job produces model artifact and JSON manifest pinned with SHA and metadata stored in artifact registry. 2) Artifact and manifest are cryptographically signed; signatures are verifiable via the provenance index. 3) Perf job runs automatically and publishes a perf-profile JSON artifact linked to the model manifest. 4) If perf passes thresholds, pipeline opens a GitOps PR against model-catalog updating pinned version for 'staged' channel; on merge, automated rollout kicks off. 5) Canary rollout monitors P50/P95 latency and correctness evals; if regression exceeds thresholds, pipeline automatically reverts the catalog pin and creates rollback notes/incident. 6) All steps produce links for auditing (PR, CI job, perf dashboard, provenance entry).
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Using deterministic builds increases confidence but requires stricter environment pinning; building reproducibly will increase CI runtime and complexity.
- Real-time profiling on large models is expensive; we will run a representative subset of workloads for canary to control cost.
- Tight gating reduces risk of regressions but slows time-to-production; we'll tune thresholds and allow explicit overrides for urgent hotfixes with audit logs.
- Storing additional provenance artifacts increases storage and retention costs; retention policy will be configurable per project.
- Automated rollback safety: false positives could cause unnecessary rollbacks; we mitigate with multiple signals (latency, quality evals, error rate) and a short cooldown window.
tasks: Define model artifact manifest schema (fields: model_sha, git_source, build_env, quantization_profile, sbom, profile_id)
Prototype signing flow using internal KMS + attestation registry (PoC integration with cosign-style workflow)
Create CI job templates: build, sign, publish artifacts; perf-run; QA tests; open GitOps PR
Implement perf-run harness inside CI and store perf results as versioned artifacts with benchmark metadata
Create gating rules and thresholds document; add automated checks to pipeline
Implement canary rollout orchestration and automated rollback job; hook into alerts and dashboarding
Add audit links to PR description: signed manifest, perf dashboard, CI logs, provenance entry
End-to-end integration tests (staging): simulate pass, simulate perf regression and validate auto-rollback
Document runtime ops playbook and incident steps for rollback investigation
notes:
Related artifacts: confluence runbook https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Model+Onboarding+CI, model-catalog PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/456 (placeholder), perf dashboard https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/model-profiles, prototype job in CI https://ci.redwood.ai/job/onboard-models/789.

Initial decision: use internal KMS for signing to meet enterprise compliance; evaluate switching to fulcio/rekor-based public attestation in Q3.

Performance gating thresholds (initial): P95 latency delta <= +10% vs baseline OR absolute P95 < 220ms for small models; throughput should not drop more than 15% for large batched workloads. These numbers will be validated during rollout.
